name: Gemma Translator
tagline: Two-person voice translator, fully offline on-device
description: Gemma Translator is an on-device, fully offline voice translator powered by Gemma 4 and LiteRT-LM, built with assistance from Google Antigravity. The two-lane kiosk interface lets two people face each other, each lane capturing speech, transcribing it with Moonshine STT, translating it with the local gemma4-e2b model, and speaking the result back through moonshine-voice TTS. The React frontend is styled for small handheld displays such as 480x320 Raspberry Pi screens, and a single deploy script turns a Raspberry Pi 5 into a permanent systemd kiosk appliance with 3D-printable case files included.
highlights: Two-lane kiosk for two people, each with its own language and push-to-talk recording
Fully on-device inference via LiteRT-LM with the gemma4-e2b model, no internet after setup
Moonshine speech-to-text and moonshine-voice text-to-speech around the translation loop
One-command Raspberry Pi 5 deployment as a permanent systemd kiosk (deploy-pi.sh)
Retro-terminal UI tuned for 480x320 displays with two keyboard modes
curatorNote: Google Creative Lab's reference hardware demo for Gemma 4: a two-person translation kiosk that runs the entire pipeline — speech-to-text, translation, and text-to-speech — on a Raspberry Pi 5 with no cloud calls. It is a concrete template for edge LLM appliances.
